Project 03 · Loyalty & subscriptions

Clube Smiles+ added streaming benefits to an existing Clube Smiles subscription.

I helped shape Clube Smiles+ from an early business proposition into a subscription experience connecting the existing Clube Smiles ecosystem with entertainment partners across plan selection, customer data, purchase, activation and ongoing management.

RoleSenior Product Designer
ScopeSubscription lifecycle, partner ecosystem, checkout, activation, design system contribution
PlatformWeb, desktop & mobile
Timeframe2026 · launched June 15, 2026

01

Business opportunity

FROM TRAVEL SUBSCRIPTION TO EVERYDAY VALUE

Smiles already had the subscription. The opportunity was to make it relevant beyond travel.

Clube Smiles already connected recurring payment, miles and travel benefits. Smiles+ introduced a new product layer on top of that relationship: entertainment benefits delivered by external partners, without replacing the customer’s existing Clube plan.

01Clube SmilesBase subscription · miles · travel benefits
+
02Smiles+Paid add-on · additional benefits
→
03Streaming benefitChoose · activate · manage · switch
THE COMPREHENSION PROBLEM Smiles+ wasn't a standalone subscription. It extended an existing one.

The experience had to make the hierarchy obvious: what customers already had, what they were adding, what they would pay for, and which benefit would be managed after purchase.

02

Market pressure

A FAMILIAR MODEL, A DIFFERENT ECOSYSTEM

Meli+ was a recurring business reference. Copying it wasn't the answer.

Bundling ecosystem benefits with entertainment was already becoming familiar in the market. The challenge was translating that logic into Smiles: a loyalty and travel ecosystem with an existing subscription, miles, recurring billing and its own commercial rules.

MARKET REFERENCEMeli+

Ecosystem subscription + external entertainment benefits.

≠
PRODUCT TRANSLATIONSmiles+

Loyalty + miles + travel + existing Clube subscription + partner benefits.

DESIGN QUESTION

How could we bring a proven subscription model into Smiles without making customers understand the complexity behind it?

03

Product complexity

ONE PRODUCT ON THE SURFACE. MANY RULES UNDERNEATH.

The interface had to absorb rules coming from Smiles, the Clube, partners, marketing and technology.

01Subscription logic

Smiles+ depended on an eligible Clube Smiles relationship and had to be understood as an additional benefit layer.

02Partner rules

Each streaming partner brought requirements for logo usage, brand presentation, banners, content and how its service could be described.

03Commercial positioning

Smiles needed to make the bundle attractive without positioning the offer in a way that competed directly with the partners' own pricing and sales narrative.

04Recurring billing

The new benefit lived on top of an existing paid relationship, so pricing, payment and plan communication had to preserve that context.

05Benefit lifecycle

Purchase was only one moment. Customers still had to choose, activate, use, manage and potentially switch their streaming benefit.

06Design System evolution

New GOL and Smiles products were converging on Tangerina while some Smiles+ needs still had no ready-made component or variant.

04

Commercial trade-off

Sell the value of the bundle without competing with the partners selling the same services.

SMILES NEEDED A proposition strong enough to compete in the market.

Make the add-on understandable, desirable and clearly worth paying for.

×
PARTNERS NEEDED Their brand and commercial positioning protected.

Respect rules around logos, banners, content, service presentation and price comparison.

DESIGN RESPONSE Compete through combined value, not a direct streaming price comparison.

The product proposition brought together Clube benefits, miles, partner choice and switching flexibility, while partner-specific content stayed inside agreed brand and commercial boundaries.

05

Cross-functional work

MY ROLE WAS ALSO TO CONNECT THE CONSTRAINTS

The product moved forward through continuous alignment, not a one-time handoff.

I worked closely with the PM, Clube Smiles leadership, Marketing, a shared Content Designer, Engineering, the Tangerina Design System team and the streaming partners.

Product + Clube leadership

Product proposition, eligibility, plan logic, commercial rules and priorities.

Streaming partners

Prototype reviews, brand rules, logos, banners, content and service presentation.

Marketing

Turning the benefit package into an attractive proposition without breaking partner constraints.

Content Design

Explaining Clube vs. Smiles+, billing, activation and supporting messages in the flow.

Tangerina Design System

Evaluating existing patterns and collaborating on new components, variants and states required by Smiles+.

Engineering

Feasibility, component behavior, tokens, implementation details and handoff.

06

Product principle

The organization could see partners, contracts, billing and systems. The customer should see one product.

Discover→Choose→Subscribe→Pay→Activate→Use→Manage→Change

This reframed the work from designing a checkout to designing the lifecycle of a subscription benefit.

01.7

A concrete iteration

The plan card changed when the offer stopped being a single plan.

The earlier composition was built around one offer. When the product needed two Smiles+ configurations, keeping that structure made comparison harder because price, streaming allowance and partner availability did not line up. I reorganized the card so both plans used the same information order and could sit side by side.

BEFOREOne offer

Benefits grouped for a standalone sales card.

CHANGETwo plan configurations

Customers now had to compare allowance, partners and monthly price.

AFTERComparable anatomy

The same content order across both cards made the differences scannable.

02

Product Experience & Decisions

FROM RULES TO A CUSTOMER JOURNEY

The product had to explain itself before asking customers to buy it.

The work connected plan comprehension, streaming choice, customer data, purchase and activation into one progression.

Understand→Compare→Choose→Confirm data→Pay→Activate

02.1

Product proposition

Show the combined value before exposing the mechanics.

Streaming was presented as an additional benefit inside the existing Smiles relationship, not as an isolated subscription.

Decision

Lead with Clube + miles + entertainment as one value proposition, then progressively explain the rules.

02.1

Partner constraints

Streaming partners reviewed how their brands and offers appeared inside Smiles+.

I presented prototypes in recurring partner reviews. Feedback covered logo use, banner presentation, service positioning and how far Smiles could go when comparing bundle value with a partner's direct offer. Those reviews changed the sales UI and copy before implementation.

SMILES NEEDEDA clear, competitive bundle
PARTNERS NEEDEDTheir direct offer and brand rules protected
DESIGN RESPONSESell the combined Clube value without turning the page into a direct price fight

02.2

Plan architecture

The plan card became the explanation layer for the product.

Customers needed to compare more than price.

01Base value

Miles + Clube benefits

02Streaming allowance

1 or 3 benefits

03Partner visibility

Options before purchase

04Recurring rule

Price + switching at decision time

02.3

Information architecture

From a standalone offer to a structure designed for comparison.

These are not default and selected states.

What changed

The hierarchy moved from presenting one offer to making differences between offers scannable.

02.4

Confirm, don't recreate

Reuse what Smiles already knows. Ask only for what the benefit needs.

The interface explicitly reassures customers that confirming email and phone for streaming access does not change their Smiles registration.

Decision

Separate benefit access data from account maintenance and explain the distinction at the moment of input.

02.5

Offer variations

Different commercial presentations, the same product hierarchy.

The layouts preserve the product hierarchy while the commercial presentation changes.

02.6

Purchase to value

Payment completes the transaction. Activation completes the customer promise.

The project material separates purchase confirmation from activation.

01PurchasedTransaction complete
→
02Benefit availableNext step is explicit
→
03ActivatedValue can be used
Product decision

Treat activation as part of the product journey, not as an external task after checkout.

02.7

Beyond acquisition

A monthly switching rule becomes a product state.

The project material establishes one streaming switch per month.

01Benefit active
→
02Switch available
→
03New benefit
→
04Switch used

The monthly switch rule comes from the project. The state sequence is a retrospective model.

02.8

Decision system

Each business rule needed a visible consequence in the experience.

Business ruleProduct decisionExperience consequence
Smiles+ extends ClubePreserve base-plan contextPlan + add-on in one hierarchy
Offers have different allowancesStandardize comparison criteriaComparable plan cards
Streaming needs contact dataConfirm without changing Smiles registrationReassurance beside the form
Purchase ≠ activationKeep activation in the journeyPost-purchase next step stays visible
One switch per monthModel switching as stateActive / available / used

04

Delivery, Measurement & Evolution

FROM FINAL UI TO IMPLEMENTABLE PRODUCT

Delivery meant making behaviour clear enough for Engineering to build without guessing.

The project delivery guidance explicitly called for final layouts with behaviour and interaction annotations, technical documentation links, Design System tokens and variables, error/loading/success states and a QA checklist when applicable.

01Final layouts

High-fidelity screens with behaviour and interaction annotations.

02Technical context

Links to supporting documentation such as Notion or Confluence.

03System language

Tangerina tokens and variables applied to the designed solution.

04Product states

Error, loading, success and other states needed for implementation.

04.1

Flow organization

The Figma file was organized to communicate hierarchy, not just screen order.

The delivery template defined the main flow horizontally, screen variations vertically, and secondary derivations in parallel.

04.2

Design → Engineering

The handoff described what changes, when it changes and what the customer can do next.

AREADESIGN SPECIFICATIONIMPLEMENTATION QUESTION

The delivery structure and state documentation requirements are evidenced in the project file.

04.3

Design QA

QA covered visual consistency, interaction behaviour and subscription rules.

The project delivery template explicitly included a QA checklist when applicable.

VISUALHierarchy & consistency

Typography, spacing, surfaces, responsive layout and Tangerina patterns.

INTERACTIONBehaviour

Selection feedback, CTA changes, loading and transition behaviour.

PRODUCTRules & states

Eligibility, activation, current benefit and monthly switching constraints.

CONTENTClarity & partner compliance

Clube vs. Smiles+ comprehension, billing language and approved partner presentation.

04.4

Expected outcomes

What we expected the new journey to improve after launch.

The product was still evolving when I left, so these are expected outcomes, not reported results.

More Clube customers adding Smiles+

Clearer plan comparison should reduce uncertainty before checkout.

More paid customers activating the benefit

Keeping activation inside the post-purchase journey should reduce the gap between payment and actual use.

Fewer support contacts about what was purchased

Explaining Clube, Smiles+, billing and partner activation at the relevant step should reduce avoidable questions.

More use of the monthly switching benefit

A visible active state and clear switching availability should make the flexibility easier to discover.

04.4

Launch measurement

LAUNCH MEASUREMENT FRAMEWORK

For a new product, success needed to be defined before enough post-launch data existed.

I don't have verified adoption, churn or retention results to attribute to this work.

NORTH-STAR CANDIDATEActivated Smiles+ subscribers

Subscribed ≠ activated ≠ receiving value.

ACQUISITIONSmiles+ adoption

Eligible Clube customers who add Smiles+.

FUNNELCheckout conversion

Plan selection → completed subscription.

VALUEStreaming activation rate

Paid subscriptions that reach active benefit.

EFFICIENCYTime to activation

How long purchase takes to become usable value.

LIFECYCLEBenefit switch rate

Whether monthly flexibility is actually used.

RETENTION6-month retention

Especially relevant where promotional conditions create a six-month commitment.

FRICTIONSupport & cancellation

Contacts related to activation, billing or benefit management, plus cancellation rate.

04.5

Product evolution

The architecture needed to survive partner and offer changes.

A subscription bundle is not static.

WHAT CAN CHANGEPartnersBrand, content and availability
WHAT CAN CHANGEOffersPrice, allowance and promotion
WHAT SHOULD REMAINProduct modelChoose → subscribe → activate → manage
WHAT SHOULD REMAINSystem logicStates, reusable components and clear rules

04.6

Reflection

The main design challenge was connecting Smiles, streaming partners, Marketing, Content, Tangerina and Engineering in one customer journey.

Smiles+ reinforced a principle I carry into complex product work.
